subject: Security exhibit — procurement checklist, redline roadmap and inspection cadence
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@healthcorp.com>

Cc: procurement@healthcorp.com, audit@healthcorp.com
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit ask + draft order form redlines

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is starting the formal review and Legal asked us to collect the security exhibit language and a proposed evidence cadence up front so we can move the order form/PO. Two quick asks:

1) Can you provide proposed redlines to the MSA security exhibit (SOC 2, pen test notification, and inspection/inspection-lite language)?
2) What cadence can you support for evidence sharing (SOC 2 reports, pen-test summaries, live evidence windows)? Our security team prefers a predictable sampling window rather than ad-hoc requests.

If you can send a short checklist and an initial redline doc today we can route internally.

Thanks —
Jane

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: procurement@healthcorp.com, audit@healthcorp.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit ask + draft order form redlines

Hi Jane —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attaching: RINF_security_redlines_v1.docx (first-pass redlines) and an evidence-cadence-template.xlsx with a proposed quarterly sampling window and a 30-day pen-test notice cadence. High-level summary:

- SOC 2: we will provide a current SOC 2 Type II report via secure link and permit annual re-receipt.
- Pen test: we share a summary report and are open to a shared pen-test window (72-hour staging window) for on-site/ephemeral access under a scoped plan.
- Inspection rights: propose "bounded inspection" language (sample sets + scheduling) rather than broad on-site access to protect multi-tenant infrastructure.
- Evidence cadence: default quarterly evidence drops + two ad-hoc windows per year for critical audits.

Ben and Karthik, could you review the redlines and weigh in on the legal/operational feasibility? Jane/procurement, we can adjust cadence based on compliance needs but want to keep the inspection scope bounded.

Attachments: RINF_security_redlines_v1.docx (redlines), evidence-cadence-template.xlsx (matrix)

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success — Assurance
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@healthcorp.com>, procurement@healthcorp.com, audit@healthcorp.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit ask + draft order form redlines

Looping in some suggested language and operational constraints — copying Jane so procurement sees the tradeoffs. (Quoted below for context.)

High-level: we want to avoid overly broad "inspection rights" that imply live access to production multi-tenant hosts. Our recommend approach:

- Replace "inspection rights" with "bounded inspection" clause that specifies scope, sampling bands (e.g., <5% sampling by account per year), and notice windows.
- Pen-test language: customer may request a pen-test; Redwood will provide a 30–60 day coordinated window on staging or ephemeral environments. We will provide a consolidated summary report and remediation timeline. Raw logs and sensitive findings will be redacted; we will provide a mechanism for controlled evidence review via secure share.
- SOC 2: provide current Type II report with an NDA; historical reports available for purchase/under subscription.

Operational asks for HealthCorp: give us your top-5 assertions (e.g., encryption-in-transit, RBAC, logging, retention, data isolation) so we can confirm the evidence bundles for the proposed quarterly drops. If you require continuous on-demand access, that becomes a higher-tier enterprise engagement (Dedicated/Private).

Proposed redline excerpt (plain text here for quick review):
"Bounded inspection: Customer may request inspection limited to pre-defined evidence types, sampling bands, and scheduled windows. Such inspections will be conducted via secure evidence transfer or ephemeral staging access; Redwood will not provide live access to production multi-tenant hosts absent a dedicated private deployment and separate agreement"

Next steps I recommend: legal sync (30 min) + ops checklist (to confirm staging capacity) + finalize language for the order form. Karthik — can you convert the docx into tracked legal redlines and flag any MSA cross-refs?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Security exhibit ask + draft order form redlines

Thanks team — quick legal/ops summary and proposed action grid. I've converted the redlines to tracked legal redlines (linked) and tightened the inspection language to make it defensible in an MSA context. Summary:

- Inspection language: final recommended clause uses the term "Evidence Review and Limited Inspection". It enumerates allowed evidence types (SOC 2 report, architecture diagrams, sanitized pen-test executive summary, log extracts limited to scoped systems) and requires 10 business days' notice for standard requests.
- Sampling bands: propose quarterly default with a 90-day rolling window; sampling limited to discrete sample sets up to 3% of total tenant endpoints per year unless otherwise negotiated.
- Pen test coordination: 30-day mutual notice for scheduled penetration tests; we will provide consolidated findings and remediation commitments (TTR windows). For high-priority critical findings, Redwood will engage a hotfix process as outlined in the SLA addendum.
- Evidence delivery: secure S3/Sharepoint link or controlled access to a read-only evidence portal. Raw PII/redacted material will not be shared without a standing DPA amendment.

Action items and owners:
1) Monica — confirm HealthCorp top-5 assertions needed (deadline: Wed 5/6 EOD).
2) Ben — finalize the executive summary template for pen-test outputs (deadline: Fri 5/8).
3) Karthik — push tracked redlines to Drive and create a one-page procurement checklist (link below) (done).
4) Jane/procurement — confirm whether the proposed quarterly cadence meets HealthCorp compliance or if they need an enterprise carve-out.

Drive (redlines + checklist): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRINF-redlines
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/HC-2026-0421

If HealthCorp is OK with the bounded approach we can proceed to sign the order form with the attached exhibit. If they push for continuous access, we'll need a dedicated/private deployment discussion and a pricing amendment. Recommend a 30-minute legal/procurement call Thursday 5/7 to land language.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
